name: Utah
overview: Utah counties sell real property with delinquent taxes at an annual tax sale that the county auditor conducts in May or June. A property is offered once its period of redemption is expiring, which comes after the lapse of four years from the date the taxes became delinquent. Until then, anyone may redeem the property on behalf of the record owner at any time before the tax sale. Each county sets its own date, format and payment rules within that window.

counties.how_to_bid: Register in person on sale day (pre-registration starts at 9:00 am) with a government-issued photo ID to receive a bidder number. Bidding is open auction to the highest bidder; the opening bid includes taxes, penalties, interest and cost of sale. The Treasurer's Department collects the successful bid and recording fee immediately after the auction closes; the FAQ lists cash, business checks or personal checks and says no financing is offered.

counties.how_to_bid: Register on PublicSurplus.com through the county's Register to Bid link and bid online. The winning bidder pays the full final bid through the online auction vendor, usually by wire transfer; the county offers no financing. Winners receive a recorded tax deed after the Utah County Commission ratifies the sale.
